extension.description: Reviews txc vault commands that disclose a stored secret, seal one to another key, widen a vault's recipients, or delete vault contents.
extension.name: txc vault command protection

permissions.description: Identifies `txc vault copy`, which decrypts a stored secret out of the vault. `--print` writes the plaintext secret to standard output, where it persists in agent transcripts and shell history; without it the secret goes to the clipboard and is cleared after a timeout.
permissions.label: txc vault secret disclosure
safer_guidance: Use `txc vault show` to confirm an entry exists; it masks every secret.
Prefer the default clipboard copy, which clears itself, over `--print`.
For an automated host, scope a single secret with a grant rather than printing it.

permissions.description: Identifies `txc vault grant`, which seals a stored secret to an arbitrary age public key. A grant is a read of the vault, so it needs no write key and is not stopped by the identity/write-key split. It is a snapshot that cannot be revoked; rotating the underlying secret is the only remedy.
permissions.label: txc vault secret grant
safer_guidance: Confirm the recipient key out of band before sealing a secret to it.
Grants cannot be revoked: rotate the secret if a grant was issued in error.
Set `--expires` for hygiene, but treat it as documentation, not enforcement.

permissions.description: Identifies txc commands that widen which keys can decrypt stored secrets: `recipients --add`, `create --recipient`, and `move`, which re-seals an entry to a destination vault whose recipient set may be larger than the source's.
permissions.label: txc vault recipient widening
safer_guidance: Run `txc vault recipients <vault>` with no flags to see the current key set first.
Verify the destination vault's recipients with `txc vault recipients <dest>` before moving an entry.
Removing a key later does not reach copies already made; rotate any secret it could read.

permissions.description: Identifies `txc vault delete`, which removes an entire vault and all its entries, and `txc vault rm`, which removes one entry. Both keep an encrypted recovery copy beside the vault, but `--yes` skips the interactive confirmation.
permissions.label: txc vault destruction
safer_guidance: Run `txc vault list <vault>` first to see what the vault still holds.
Omit `--yes` so the command asks for the vault's name before deleting it.
`delete` removes a whole vault; `rm` removes a single entry.

rules.description: Identifies `txc vault copy --print`, which writes a decrypted secret to standard output instead of the self-clearing clipboard. The documented use is command substitution into an environment variable, which leaves the plaintext in the surrounding process and in any transcript of the session.
safer_alternatives: Drop `--print` to use the clipboard copy, which clears after `--clear-after` seconds.
Use `txc vault show` when you only need to confirm the entry exists.
rules.title: txc vault secret printed to standard output

rules.description: Identifies `txc vault copy` without `--print`, which decrypts a stored secret onto the system clipboard. The clipboard is readable by any process running as the user until it is cleared.
safer_alternatives: Use `txc vault show` to confirm an entry exists without decrypting its secret.
Lower `--clear-after` to shorten the window the secret stays on the clipboard.
rules.title: txc vault secret copied to the clipboard

rules.description: Identifies `txc vault grant`, which seals one stored secret to another age public key. txc documents this as a read of the vault that needs no write key, so the identity/write-key split does not contain it, and a grant cannot be revoked.
safer_alternatives: Confirm the recipient key out of band before sealing a secret to it.
Rotate the underlying secret if a grant was issued in error; grants cannot be revoked.
rules.title: txc vault secret sealed to another key

rules.description: Identifies `txc vault recipients --add`, which re-seals every secret in a vault to an additional age public key, granting that key permanent read access to the vault's current contents.
safer_alternatives: Run `txc vault recipients <vault>` with no flags to review the current key set.
Confirm the added key's fingerprint out of band before re-sealing.
rules.title: txc vault re-sealed to an additional key

rules.description: Identifies `txc vault create --recipient`, which creates a vault already encrypted to an external age public key, so every secret later added to it is readable by that key.
safer_alternatives: Create the vault with no `--recipient` and add keys deliberately afterwards.
Confirm the recipient key's fingerprint out of band first.
rules.title: txc vault created for an additional key

rules.description: Identifies `txc vault move`, which decrypts an entry and seals it again to the destination vault's keys. txc documents that the destination's key set may differ from the source's, so a move can widen who can read the entry.
safer_alternatives: Check the destination with `txc vault recipients <dest>` before moving an entry.
Move into a vault you own rather than one shared with additional keys.
rules.title: txc vault entry re-sealed into another vault

rules.description: Identifies `txc vault delete`, which removes an entire vault and every entry in it. A `.deleted` recovery copy is kept beside the vault, and `--yes` skips the prompt that would otherwise ask for the vault's name.
safer_alternatives: Run `txc vault list <vault>` first to see what the vault still holds.
Omit `--yes` so the command asks for the vault's name before deleting it.
rules.title: txc vault deleted

rules.description: Identifies `txc vault rm`, which removes a single entry from a vault. The previous vault version is kept encrypted in a `.bak` file only until the next change, and `--yes` skips the confirmation.
safer_alternatives: Run `txc vault show <entry>` first to confirm which entry is being removed.
Omit `--yes` so the removal is confirmed interactively.
rules.title: txc vault entry removed

safer_alternatives: Use `txc vault list` and `txc vault show` to inspect the vault; both keep secrets masked.
Confirm a recipient or grant key's fingerprint out of band before sealing secrets to it.
Prefer the self-clearing clipboard copy over `--print` when a secret must leave the vault.
